title: Determining freshwater pCO2 based on geochemical calculation and modelling using PHREEQC
author: Pötter, Tollrian, et al.

steps.title: Prepare M4 medium
steps.instruction: Dissolve the following components in de‑ionised water to obtain the final M4 medium (per litre): CaCl₂·2H₂O 29.38 g · 100 ml⁻¹ (1.0 ml l⁻¹), MgSO₄ 24.66 g · 100 ml⁻¹ (0.5 ml l⁻¹), KCl 5.80 g · 100 ml⁻¹ (0.1 ml l⁻¹), NaHCO₃ 6.48 g · 100 ml⁻¹ (1.0 ml l⁻¹), Na₂SiO₃·9H₂O 2.50 g · 100 ml⁻¹ (0.2 ml l⁻¹), NaNO₃ 0.27 g · 100 ml⁻¹ (0.1 ml l⁻¹), KH₂PO₄ 0.07 g · 100 ml⁻¹ (0.1 ml l⁻¹), K₂HPO₄ 0.18 g · 100 ml⁻¹ (0.1 ml l⁻¹). Adjust the final volume to 1 L.

steps.title: Collect and condition sample
steps.instruction: Take a representative freshwater sample for analysis. Record the sample mass if needed (e.g., m₁ = 184.36 g and 160.19 g; m₂ = 84.36 g and 60.17 g) and keep the sample at ambient temperature until analysis.

steps.title: Measure pH and temperature
steps.instruction: Using an LL‑Aquatrode plus Pt 1000 F/4 mm electrode (Metrohm AG, Herisau, Switzerland), measure the pH of the sample (two readings: 6.44 and 6.363; mean pH = 6.406) and the temperature (two readings: 22.32 °C and 21.9 °C; mean temperature = 22.10 °C). Record the values.

steps.title: Perform endpoint titration
steps.instruction: Determine acid capacity (KS 4.3) and base capacity (KB 8.2) by endpoint titration:

substeps.instruction: Add NaOH/HCl titrant to the sample; record the volume of titrant added for each replicate (V₁ = 0.862 ml and 0.926 ml).
Record the endpoint pH values (8.25 and 4.28).
Measure the second titration volume (V₂ = 100.00 ml and 100.02 ml).
Calculate acid capacity KS 4.3 = 0.926 mmol L⁻¹ and base capacity KB 8.2 = 0.862 mmol L⁻¹.

steps.title: Calculate TCO₂ and alkalinity
steps.instruction: From the titration data compute total CO₂ concentration (TCO₂) = 78.664 mg L⁻¹ and total alkalinity (TA) = 46.341 mg L⁻¹ for the sample.

steps.title: Set up PHREEQC input
steps.instruction: Create a PHREEQC input file containing:

substeps.instruction: Keyword C(4) as CO₂ with the measured TCO₂ value.
Keyword Alkalinity with the measured TA value.
Optional: all additional hydro‑geochemical and physical parameters (full‑parameter run).

steps.title: Run PHREEQC with full parameters
steps.instruction: Execute PHREEQC using the input file that includes pH, TCO₂ or TA, temperature, density, and the full set of hydro‑geochemical and physical parameters (denoted “+”). Verify that the calculated ion‑balance error ≤ 5 % (acceptable). Record the resulting pCO₂ value.

steps.title: Run PHREEQC with limited parameters
steps.instruction: Optionally, run PHREEQC with a reduced input containing only pH, TCO₂ or TA, temperature and density (denoted “–”). Expect an ion‑balance error ≥ 99 % and note the deviation of the calculated pCO₂ from the full‑parameter result.

steps.title: Assess ion‑balance error
steps.instruction: For each PHREEQC run compute the ion‑balance error as (100 × (cations − anions))/(cations + anions). Accept results only if the error is ≤ 5 % for the full‑parameter analysis; otherwise re‑examine the analytical data (e.g., missing ions or concentration errors).
